## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying:
- dd-3: Concurrent invocation of mutation-append (or churn-append) for two distinct PRs produces exactly two entries — no duplicates, no lost entries
- dd-4: Test simulates two concurrent appends (background subshells racing on same tracking ticket) and asserts both entries land exactly once

Create tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh that simulates concurrent PR-merge appends:

  Run two mutation-append invocations in background subshells with different PR numbers (&):
    DSO=<stub> calibration-report.sh mutation-append --pr=101 --findings-file=f1.json &
    DSO=<stub> calibration-report.sh mutation-append --pr=102 --findings-file=f2.json &
    wait

  Assert that the stub DSO records exactly 2 ticket-comment calls (one per PR), no duplicates.

Use a dso stub (PATH-prepended) that records all ticket-comment invocations to a temp file. After both subshells complete, verify:
  - Exactly 2 comment lines recorded (not 1 or 3+)
  - Line for PR 101 present exactly once
  - Line for PR 102 present exactly once

Also test the idempotency guard under concurrency: two subshells with the SAME PR number race → exactly 1 comment recorded (not 2).

## Testing Mode
RED — write the concurrency test first; it passes once mutation-append's idempotency guard handles concurrent same-PR calls correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Concurrent different-PR test: exactly 2 comment calls — Verify: bash tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh
- Test file is executable — Verify: test -x tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh
- Test uses mktemp for all temp files — Verify: grep -q 'mktemp' tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh

## File Impact
- tests/scripts/test-calibration-concurrent-append.sh — Create
data.title: Test concurrent mutation-append and churn-append invocations produce exactly two entries
